chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: Linton Garner and Erroll's European poll
summary: Collins met Erroll's brother Linton during a big show with Nat and Duke, and confirms Garner's poll win rested on his Slam Stewart recordings and the Paris engagement lasted three weeks.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: now. Where are we? We were in Pittsburgh. (inaudible). How about Linton Garner?

I didn't know Linton. I met Linton in later years when Linton was an accompanist for Timmy Rogers. Linton was a very good pianist also, but I didn't -- Billy Strayhorn used to talk about Linton because they were friends.
Yeah, I didn't meet Linton until we were doing the big show with Nat and Duke, Duke Ellington.
Yeah, '50, '51, around that time. And Linton -- then I met Linton. Very good pianist. Quite different from Earl though, you know, had his own style. But --
You were talking about in Europe how he'd won a poll in Europe.
On the basis of recordings (inaudible). of recordings with Slam Stewart.
That he had done with Slam Stewart, yeah. And --
And where else did you play in Europe?

That particular time I only played Paris, you know, and we would go -- just for say about three weeks. Paris was beautiful then too, you know, this wide open, just lovely. But my next trip to Europe was with Nat
